content.text: Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail

Stripe's 46-country limitation and PayPal's account suspension policies are well-documented, but what's not as well-known is that these platforms can hold funds for up to 180 days, without appeal, or deny access outright, leaving digital creators high and dry. This infrastructure is designed to bypass these restrictions, giving you control over your own commerce ecosystem, with no platform to depend on, no subscriptions, and lifetime access to a sovereign digital commerce stack. By [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/how-building-crypto-store-cloudflare-pages-works-how-6|COREMERCH guide to building]] a sovereign digital commerce stack, you're not just avoiding platform restrictions, you're also future-proofing your business, ensuring it remains resilient and adaptable to any regulatory or economic changes in your market.
What You Need Before You Deploy

Before deploying your sovereign digital commerce stack, you'll need to acquire a domain name, set up a GitHub or Cloudflare Pages account for hosting, and obtain a NOWPayments account for automatic crypto payment processing. You'll also need to choose a programming language and a backend framework, such as Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script. Additionally, you'll need to select a storage solution, such as Supabase or Google Sheets, and a file delivery mechanism, like Google Drive or Cloudflare R2. By having these components in place, you'll be able to build a robust and scalable digital commerce ecosystem that's tailored to your specific needs.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

To set up your payment and delivery pipeline, you'll need to integrate NOWPayments with your chosen storage solution and file delivery mechanism. This will allow you to automatically process payments and deliver digital products to your customers. You'll also need to configure your backend framework to handle payment notifications and delivery requests. By setting up this pipeline, you'll be able to efficiently and securely process transactions and deliver digital products to your customers, without relying on third-party platforms.
Building a sovereign digital commerce stack requires careful planning and execution.
Going Live and Processing Your First Transaction

Once your payment and delivery pipeline is set up, you can go live with your sovereign digital commerce stack. To process your first transaction, you'll need to create a new payment endpoint, configure your NOWPayments account, and integrate your storage solution and file delivery mechanism. By following these steps, you'll be able to process your first transaction and start selling digital products without relying on Stripe or other platforms that can be restrictive or unreliable.
Scaling Once the Infrastructure Is Running

The storefront in a COREMERCH deployment is a static site hosted on GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages. It costs nothing to host. It scales to any traffic level automatically. It cannot be taken down by a payment platform's compliance decision because the hosting and the payment layer are completely separate infrastructure. Your buyer experience is clean and professional — a product page, a crypto checkout with QR code generation and live price feeds, and an automatic delivery email within 30 seconds of payment. Every component runs under your own accounts. If COREMERCH closed tomorrow, every store deployed would continue running exactly as it does today. That is what infrastructure ownership means.
